title: Sepak Takraw: overview
d: Sepak Takraw is a team net sport played 3 per side (regu).
definition: Sepak Takraw is a team net sport played 3 per side (regu).
description: Sepak Takraw is a team net sport. score more points than the opponent. The contest is played 3 per side (regu), and the side that rally scoring to 21 (win by 2); best of 3 sets wins. Southeast Asian origins; ISTAF governs; Thailand and Malaysia dominate world play. The sport is governed by official laws that cover the field of play, equipment, players, officials, scoring, fouls, and conduct; this database walks through every one of those areas so a newcomer can follow a full match with understanding.

title: The objective
d: The objective of Sepak Takraw is: score more points than the opponent.
definition: The objective of Sepak Takraw is: score more points than the opponent.
description: Every rule in Sepak Takraw exists to serve one objective: score more points than the opponent. All tactics, positions, and scoring flow from that single aim. Beginners should fix the objective in mind first, because every foul, stoppage, and strategy in the sport is judged against whether it fairly advances or unfairly blocks that objective. Coaches return to it constantly: if a play does not serve the objective, it is the wrong play.

Tiebreak rules are announced before play and never invented mid-game; players and coaches must know them, because they reshape tactics — a team may play for penalties, or gamble everything to avoid them.

Timekeeping is an official duty — the clock, not the players, decides when it ends, and added or extra time exists to compensate for stoppages so the advertised duration is genuinely played.

Break length and number are fixed by the rules; exceeding them can draw penalties.

definition: Substitution rules in Sepak Takraw control how and when players may be replaced.

definition: The referee in Sepak Takraw enforces the laws, keeps time, and manages conduct.

title: Fouls
d: Illegal play in Sepak Takraw draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
definition: Illegal play in Sepak Takraw draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
description: A foul in Sepak Takraw is illegal play as defined by the laws — not just rough play, but any act the rules forbid. Officials grade fouls by intent, danger, and advantage gained; persistent or cynical fouling draws escalating punishment. Smart players learn the exact line: physical right up to it, never across it.

title: Penalties
d: Fouls in Sepak Takraw are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
definition: Fouls in Sepak Takraw are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
description: Punishment in Sepak Takraw fits the foul: minor infringements restart play for the other side, serious ones award direct scoring chances or remove the offender. Penalty rules are deliberately severe enough that fouling is never a good trade — the team that stays disciplined keeps eleven (or its equivalent) on the field and wins the close ones.

description: The laws of Sepak Takraw punish misconduct on a ladder: warnings, cards, sin-bins, ejections, suspensions. Dissent, dangerous play, and unsporting behavior are treated as seriously as technical fouls, because the game depends on respect for officials and opponents. Captains are responsible for their team's conduct and speak to the referee for the side.
